claims.title: Polynesian voyagers settle Aotearoa
claims.summary: The ancestors of the Māori reached New Zealand from East Polynesia in great voyaging canoes around 1300 CE, making it one of the last large landmasses on Earth to be permanently settled.

claims.title: The Māori world takes shape
claims.summary: Settlers adapted to a temperate land and developed the distinct Māori culture of iwi and hapū, organised by whakapapa and rangatira and expressed through carving, weaving, and the working of pounamu.

claims.title: Settlement of the Chatham Islands
claims.summary: Māori reached the remote Chatham Islands (Rēkohu) over 750 km east of the mainland, where the settlers became the distinct Moriori people with their own traditions.

claims.title: Abel Tasman sights New Zealand
claims.summary: The Dutch navigator Abel Tasman became the first European to sight New Zealand, charting a fragment of the west coast but leaving without landing after a deadly clash with Māori in Golden Bay.

claims.summary: Samuel Marsden conducted New Zealand's first Christian service at Rangihoua in the Bay of Islands, beginning the missionary presence that spread Christianity, literacy, and new ideas among Māori.

claims.title: The musket wars
claims.summary: The spread of firearms unleashed a generation of devastating inter-tribal warfare, with leaders such as Te Rauparaha driving migrations and conquests that killed tens of thousands and reshaped the tribal map.

claims.title: The New Zealand Wars
claims.summary: Disputes over land and sovereignty erupted into war in Taranaki in 1860 and spread across the North Island, pitting imperial and colonial forces against iwi defending their land and autonomy until about 1872.

claims.title: Land confiscation legalised (raupatu)
claims.summary: The New Zealand Settlements Act 1863 gave a legal cloak to the confiscation of about 1.2 million hectares of Māori land, chiefly in the Waikato and Taranaki, often taking land from iwi who had not fought the Crown.

claims.summary: New Zealand became the first self-governing nation in the world to grant women the parliamentary vote, the culmination of a petition campaign led by Kate Sheppard and the temperance movement.

claims.summary: The Treaty of Waitangi Act 1975 created the Waitangi Tribunal to investigate Crown breaches of the Treaty's principles; in 1985 its mandate was extended back to 1840, enabling redress for historic wrongs.
